newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria appoints Total as downstream oil advisor.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria appoints Total as downstream oil advisor.

text.p: Nigeria's military government has appointed Total Nigeria as a consultant on downstream operations in the oil industry, the failure of which has led to paralysing fuel shortages.
A statement from the Ministry of Petroleum Resources in the capital Abuja said the announcement of Total's appointment was made on Tuesday by oil minister Dan Etete.
"Government is concerned about the problems facing the sector and is determined to find an early and lasting solution," the statement said.
Total Nigeria is a petroleum products marketing company which is majority-owned by France's Total.

The failure of poorly-maintained refineries to work close to their designed capacity of 445,000 barrels per day, as well as of the distribution network, has led to bouts of fuel scarcity which paralyse Africa's biggest crude oil producer for weeks at a time.
Local business and the World Bank have said that the best long term solution is to privatise the sector, but the military government appears reluctant to do so.
Refineries complain that they are not given sufficient funds to operate efficiently and complain that the margin they receive from the subsidised sale of refined products is too small.
